## Pull request overview

This PR addresses multiple ROADMAP items across DX/UX/docs by completing console i18n coverage, polishing CLI diagnostics/validation, enriching deprecation warnings with migration snippets, and adding several new documentation guides and README examples.

**Changes:**
- Completed console i18n keys and migrated UI strings (ModeToggle, ObjectView, ErrorBoundary) plus added a LocaleSwitcher in the header.
- Improved CLI commands (`doctor`, `dev`, `check`) and expanded deprecation warnings with migration guidance links.
- Added multiple new docs pages and expanded README with schema examples; updated ROADMAP status.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 29 out of 30 changed files in this pull request and generated 14 comments.

These SchemaRenderer examples use `type: 'ObjectGrid'` and `object: 'task'`, but the actual ObjectQL grid schema type is `object-grid` with `objectName` (see `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`). The current example will fail schema resolution unless updated to the real type string and property names.
```suggestion
          type: 'object-grid',
          objectName: 'task',
```

The guide says plugins are driven by JSON schemas, but the `BoardSchema` example includes `onItemMove?: (itemId, toColumnId) => void`, which isn’t JSON-serializable and can’t come from a server-driven schema. Consider modeling this as declarative `events`/`actions` (or document it explicitly as an in-code-only escape hatch) to avoid confusing users about what can be represented in JSON.

TypeScript version parsing can mis-detect valid versions (e.g. ranges like `>=5`, `workspace:*`, or `latest`) because it strips non-digits and `parseInt`s the first segment. If `majorVer` becomes `NaN`, the command will emit a misleading warning. Consider using a semver parser/coercion (or at least guarding `Number.isFinite(majorVer)` before comparing) and report when the version string can’t be interpreted.

This section states `@object-ui/types` has “no runtime code” and “zero runtime dependencies”, but the package ships JS (`dist/*.js`) and has runtime deps like `zod` and `@objectstack/spec` in `packages/types/package.json`. Please adjust the architecture description to reflect the actual dependency/runtime characteristics.

The `BoardImpl` example uses an inline `style={{ gridTemplateColumns: ... }}`. This conflicts with the project’s Tailwind-first approach and makes theming/overrides harder. Consider showing a Tailwind-based solution (e.g., fixed `grid-cols-*`, or a CSS variable + Tailwind utility) so the example aligns with ObjectUI’s styling conventions.
```suggestion
    <div className={cn('grid grid-flow-col auto-cols-fr gap-4 overflow-x-auto', className)}>
```

The Kanban example schema appears to mix multiple schema styles (`type: 'kanban'` plus `objectName/groupBy/titleField`), but `KanbanSchema` in `@object-ui/types` expects a `columns: KanbanColumn[]` structure, while the ObjectQL-backed variant is `type: 'object-kanban'` with different required fields (see `packages/types/src/complex.ts` vs `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`). Please align the example with one real schema so it validates and renders.

`knownTypes` is missing valid built-in schema types (e.g. `object-grid`, `object-form`, `object-kanban`, `object-calendar`, etc. from `@object-ui/types`), so `objectui check` will warn on schemas that are actually valid. Consider validating `content` via the Zod schemas in `@object-ui/types/zod` (e.g. `SchemaNodeSchema` / `ObjectQLComponentSchema`) or expand the list to match the real type unions.

The German translation has mismatched quotation marks around `{{objectName}}` (opens with `„` but closes with `"`). This will render oddly in the UI; use matching quotes (e.g. `„{{objectName}}“` or plain `"{{objectName}}"`).
```suggestion
      objectNotFoundDescription: 'Das Objekt „{{objectName}}“ existiert in der aktuellen Konfiguration nicht.',
```

This doc snippet uses `ThemeProvider defaultTheme="system"`, but `ThemeProvider`’s API expects `defaultTheme` to be a theme *name* (e.g. `"light"`) and uses `defaultMode` for `light|dark|auto`. Using `system` here won’t work with the current `ThemeProvider` implementation in `packages/react/src/context/ThemeContext.tsx`.
```suggestion
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light" defaultMode="system">
```
